note.explanation: Significant figures show which digits in a measurement are reliably known, including the first doubtful digit. Count all digits from 1 to 9. A zero between non-zero digits counts, a zero at the left does not, and a zero at the right of a decimal does. In scientific notation, count the digits before the exponent.
note.simple: Significant figures are the measurement digits we can rely on, plus the first estimated digit. Count carefully: some zeros count and some do not.
note.checkQuestion: How many significant figures are there in 0.0034 m?
note.title: Counting Significant Figures
steps: Count a zero between two digits.
Do not count zeros on the left side of a measured value.
Count zeros on the right side of a decimal.
In scientific notation, count all digits before the exponent.
note.answer: Significant figures are the reliably known digits in a measurement, including the first doubtful digit.
